item.title: Python Applied Mathematics Labs
item.description:
📝 What You’ll Learn# Core Technical Skills# Python libraries: NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, pandas, and other scientific packages Core mathematical algorithms, numerical methods, and modeling techniques Coding best practices, including unit testing and code optimization Array broadcasting and efficient numerical computation Data visualization and analysis techniques Real-World Applications# In these labs, you will solve problems such as: Predicting tsunami landing times using Dijkstra’s algorithm Optimizing meal plans on a budget with linear programming Cleaning and filtering sound files using Fourier transforms and convolutions Denoising images using matrix decompositions and calculus of variations Facial recognition Compressing images with matrix decompositions and wavelets Building text generators using Markov chains Creating recommendation systems with non-negative matrix factorization Creating and training machine learning models using several methods[2] Training neural networks Using information theory to beat the NYT game Wordle Modeling population dynamics with SIR and predator-prey models Site Structure# At the top of each page, you’ll find several useful tools: Fig. Environment Setup — Step-by-step instructions to configure your system for the ACME labs. Supplemental Labs — Optional labs introducing additional concepts.
🔗 Read more: https://labs.acme.byu.edu/Pages/intro.html
